SetSourceRequest.description:
`source.set`: a full state assignment for one source.

Every field is optional and only what is named moves, which is how every
other setter in this protocol works. The one that matters here is `place`:
it moves a running source between the core, a sidecar and a node.

Unknown fields are refused rather than dropped. Serde's default is to
ignore what it does not recognise, and a setter that answers 200 to a field
it threw away is indistinguishable from one that saved it: the first party
drawer sent `uri` here for months and told the operator it was saved.

color.description:
The colour the UI and the tally show it in. On the scene document,
like the name.

id.description:
Source id. `source` is accepted too, which is what the scene side of
this method has always been called with.

latency_ms.description: The latency budget in milliseconds, answered on the LATENCY query.

name.description:
What to call it in the UI. Kept on the scene document, so every
client, the tally and an agent read the same name.

params.description: Params for the source's own kind. Merged over what it has.

transport.description: How a remote source's media travels: `rtp`, `srt` or `whip`.

Severity.description: How much the reader should care.

oneOf.description: The scene will not composite as written.
It will composite, and it is probably not what was meant.
Worth knowing before going to air.

SnapshotRequest.description: `snapshot.get` on `/rpc` and through MCP. The REST route serves the same bytes raw, because an `` tag cannot read base64 out of JSON.

allow_large.description: Permit a width above the `[snapshot] max_width` ceiling.

force.description: Ignore the per client rate limit for this one request.

id.description: "sheet", "program", or a source id. A `.jpg` on the end is accepted.

width.description:
Scale down to this many pixels across, keeping the aspect. Never
enlarges. Omit for the `[snapshot] default_width` of 320, which is
enough to see who is in shot; `width: 0` for the cell's own size.

SourceAudioState.description:
What a source's audio controls read back as, which is what the audio
endpoint answers with.

Wider than `SourceAudio` because the fader and the mute apply to every
source, while the page and media balance belongs only to a superimposed one.
Every number here is read off the elements after the request landed, so a
request whose gain was clamped answers with the gain that took effect.

page.description:
Absent on anything but a superimposed source, which is the only kind
with separate sounds to balance.

SourceMeta.description: A source's name, colour and tray folder, as this collection has them.

color.description:
Free text so a client can use whatever it draws with. Absent means the
client picks one by kind.

group.description:
A tray folder: a tag on the source, purely for finding things. Not a
scene group, which is a thing on the canvas.

SourcePositionState.description:
Where a seekable source has got to, which is what the seek endpoint answers
with.

Both numbers are read back off the pipeline after the seek has landed, not
taken from the request. A seek snaps to a key unit, so the frame an operator
asked for and the frame they got are rarely the same millisecond, and a
scrubber drawn from the request would sit a little away from the picture.

duration_ms.description: Absent while the demuxer has not worked the duration out yet.

SourceReport.description: One line of the report: an OBS source and what happened to it.

oneOf.description: It came across whole.
It came across, and the plugin that plays it is not installed yet.

It did not come across. `placeholder` names what was put in the scene
in its place, when anything was.

obs_type.description: The OBS plugin type, for example `ffmpeg_source`.

placements.description: How many items in the collection use it.

oneOf.description: Pipeline is up but no media has arrived yet.
Buffers arriving within the stall timeout.

Was live, then went quiet. Its program pad is held at alpha 0 so the
slate shows through rather than a frozen frame.
The input pipeline errored. A retry is scheduled.

audio_idle_ms.description:
Same for audio. `None` here while `has_audio` is true means the source
advertised an audio track that never produced a decoded sample.

cell.description: Index into the multiview grid, or None while the source has no cell.

gain.description:
The operator's fader for this source, 0.0 silent through 1.0 unity to a
ceiling of 10.0. Read back off the volume element rather than remembered,
so what the UI shows is what the pipeline is doing.

muted.description:
Muted by the operator. Held apart from the fader so that unmuting returns
the source to where it was rather than to unity.

position_ms.description:
Where this source has got to, and how long it runs, in milliseconds.
`None` on anything not seekable, and on a seekable source whose duration
the demuxer has not worked out yet.

seekable.description:
True when this source can be scrubbed. A file can be. A camera, an RTMP
feed or a page cannot, and asking one to is a mistake worth refusing
rather than quietly doing nothing.

video_idle_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last video buffer, or None if none has arrived.

at_running_time_ms.description: Programme running time the cut landed on.

by.description: Token id that asked for it, or "core" when the mixer did it itself.

seq.description: Event sequence number the take was published under.

source.description: What went on air. Null is the slate.

at_running_time_ms.description:
Programme running time to land the cut on, in milliseconds. Omit for
immediate. Read the current running time from `core.info` or a status
snapshot first.

scene.description:
The scene to take, by name or by id. `source` wins when both are
given; with neither, the armed scene goes on air.

source.description: Id of the source to put on air.

transition.description: "fade", or {type, duration_ms, params}. Absent is a cut.

task_id.description:
The id a long running method answered with. Spelled `id` on the REST
route, where it is in the path, and `task_id` everywhere else, which
is what 03 section 6 calls it.

age_secs.description: Seconds since the task was started.

kind.description:
The method that started it, so a client reading a list knows what it is
looking at.

poll_interval_ms.description: How long to wait before asking again, while it is still running.

progress.description: 0 to 1 where the work can say, absent where it cannot.

result.description: The body the method would have answered with, once it is done.

TokenInfo.description:
What the calling token is allowed to do, echoed back so a surface can grey
out what it cannot reach instead of discovering it at the first refusal.

confirm.description: "none" or "required": whether destructive calls need a confirm token.

profile.description: MCP tool profile this token is meant for: "standard" or "minimal".

arguments.description: The tool's own arguments, as its input schema describes them.

name.description: `<plugin>/<tool>`, or the bare tool name when only one plugin has it.

Transform.description: Where an item sits and how it is sized.

anchor.description:
Normalised 0 to 1 within the item's own box: (0,0) top left, (0.5,0.5)
centre, (1,1) bottom right.

frame.description:
The rectangle the content is fitted into, in canvas pixels. Absent
means the content's own size, scaled.

position.description: Canvas pixels, of the item's anchor point.

Transition2.description: A named transition between two scenes.

TransitionRequest.description: How a take gets there. See docs/reference/transitions.md.

duration_ms.description: How long it takes. 0 is a cut.

params.description: A stinger takes clip, cut_at_ms, luma.

type.description: cut, fade, move, stinger, or a plugin name.

UiDefaults.description:
What a surface starts with: the layout, the theme and the gallery mode.

Chosen by a preset (`preset.apply`), carried in `core.info` and pushed as
`event/ui.changed`. None of it changes what the core does. It exists so the
first page a volunteer sees is the one their preset chose rather than the
one the last person to use this browser chose. 05 section 3b is where the
four gallery modes are defined.

gallery.description:
`live`, `snapshot`, `icon` or `label`. Absent means the surface asks
the machine, which is what `gmx doctor` proposes.

layout.description: Slot to panels, top to bottom. Empty means the surface's own default.

preset.description: The preset that set these, so a surface knows one has been applied.

theme.description: A theme id the surface resolves, for example `dark` or `calm`.

Update.description: One record as it was and as it is.

source.description:
Where the new build comes from. Defaults to wherever this plugin was
installed from last time.

scene.description: Leave it out to check the whole collection.

ok.description: True when there is nothing to fix.

Vec2.description: A point or a pair of factors.

bearer.description: The control token. A GET may carry it as ?token= instead, because a browser opening a WebSocket or an tag cannot set a header.

info.description:
Generated from the method table in crates/godwinmix-protocol/. api_level 1, compatible from 1. The same methods are reachable over JSON-RPC on the /rpc WebSocket; see protocol.md. The paths here come from the noun.verb transform rule, so `source.list` is `GET /api/v1/sources` and `source.audio.set` is `POST /api/v1/sources/{id}/audio`.

Four keys are accepted in the body of every call: `trace_id`, `idempotency_key` on anything mutating, `dry_run` on anything destructive, and `confirm` where the token's policy requires it.
